title: Basel III: international regulatory framework for banks
summary: This page is an index/portal to Basel III framework documents. It lists document titles and dates but contains no substantive analysis, data, or policy content itself.
key_points: Basel III standards are minimum requirements applying to internationally active banks
Post-crisis regulatory reforms were endorsed by the GHOS oversight body on 7 December 2017
Adjustments to the market risk framework were endorsed on 14 January 2019
Key components include: minimum capital requirements for market risk, Liquidity Coverage Ratio, and Net Stable Funding Ratio
Member jurisdictions are committed to implementing standards within established timeframes
why_it_matters: Basel III standards shape the regulatory environment for globally active banks, affecting capital buffers, liquidity requirements, and risk management practices. These frameworks influence market structure by constraining leverage and mandating resilience measures that affect how banks interact with financial markets.
macro_context: The Basel III framework represents the international regulatory response to systemic vulnerabilities exposed during the 2007-09 financial crisis. By strengthening capital requirements and liquidity standards, these measures aim to reduce the probability of bank failures and contagion risks that amplify macro-financial shocks.
market_structure_context: The Basel III market risk framework directly affects how banks position themselves in trading operations, influencing liquidity provision and market depth. The Liquidity Coverage Ratio and Net Stable Funding Ratio mandate specific funding profiles that shape bank behavior across asset classes.
